A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E-GSM, CoRe and extension work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original human evaluations, problem-length analyses, prompting experiments, supervised fine-tuning results and transfer evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds annotator-agreement statistics, semantic/reasoning diagnostics, an error analysis and additional model evaluations.

M1.justification: V2's CoRe corresponds to v1's CoRe plus zero-shot CoT, retaining the condition-retrieval-then-reasoning procedure. Iterative extension and supervised fine-tuning on D0 union D1 remain. Narrowing the presented prompting variants and correcting the displayed loss do not establish a different underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, its E-GSM extensions, MAWPS, SVAMP and GSM-IC for the same mathematical tasks and context conditions. The new diagnostics and newer-model evaluations use existing coverage; no additional dataset, domain or distinct task scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Self-consistency and CoRe-plus-PS/PS+ comparisons disappear. Transfer experiments replace unfine-tuned baselines with fine-tuning without extension, and Mistral gains a D0-only control. LLaMA-2's D0 control already appeared in v1 Table 16, so its appearance in v2 Table 2 is relocation rather than a newly introduced comparator.

E3.justification: V2 introduces semantic/reasoning metrics and a 50-error sampling protocol, adds GPT-4o-mini to E-GSM evaluation and removes several configurations, including LLaMA-3. The reported solvability filter changes from two models using six prompts each to three models using four each (v1 Section 2.3; v2 Appendix A.4). Identical retained question counts do not establish whether filtering was rerun. Existing dataset splits and SFT budgets remain.

E4.justification: V2 Section 4.3 and Figure 4 add analyses separating semantic understanding from reasoning across extension rounds. Appendix B.2 adds a 50-case failure audit, while Appendix F repeats the length analysis with GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o and o1. Existing training curves, data-scaling ablations and worked cases are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 newly reports pairwise Cohen's kappa for binary and three-class annotation judgments. Neither version reports repeated-training uncertainty or confidence intervals. Appendix F extends the existing Mann-Whitney testing practice to additional models rather than introducing a new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o-mini, Mistral-D0, transfer-control and diagnostic results while removing several prompting and LLaMA-3 result sets. Reported values also change: Gemini zero-shot CoT CoLeG-E goes from 49.20 to 49.16, and GPT-3.5-turbo CoRe GSM-IC accuracy from 90.05 to 89.60. The 14 retained specialist comparisons and scaling table match numerically. Changed baseline gains are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the displayed loss from positive log likelihood to negative log likelihood and corrects the answer/path indexing in the augmented-data definition. These are limited formal corrections consistent with the retained training description. Neither version develops substantive theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add an explanatory contribution: improvements arise from better reasoning pathways rather than improved semantic understanding. They explicitly expand the research question to what drives accuracy gains. The original E-GSM, CoRe, extension and generalization contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets its diagnostics as showing that reasoning improves while semantic understanding remains largely unchanged, and hypothesizes that understanding is principally established during pretraining. It also expands interpretation of efficacy versus robustness. V1's explicit limitations discussion covering dataset quality, generalizability, training-data scale and interpretability is removed, although some related caveats remain elsewhere.

D1.justification: V2 identifies all-mpnet-base-v2 for the new diagnostics and discloses annotators' mathematics training and educational levels. Conversely, Appendix B.1 removes model identifiers and access details for several specialist models whose results remain. Core prompts, SFT hyperparameters, hardware, computation estimates and repository disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds ROSCOE, FActScore, robustness-benchmark references and an explicit comparison with DUP prompting, distinguishing CoRe's additional instruction from DUP's three-stage approach. These are localized positioning additions; the main related-work framework remains. The citation-style conversion is a presentation change.

P1.justification: The abstract, methodological explanation and results narrative undergo substantial rewriting. Quality-control details move to Appendix A.4, experimental setup moves into Section 4, and proprietary/open-source results are reorganized around combined main results and separate diagnostic and specialist-model discussions. Appendices are also reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 restructures the main comparison into a consolidated table with all extension-round accuracies, redesigns the transfer table and consolidates specialist tables. V1 Figures 4 and 5 become a combined figure. New displays include the eight-panel diagnostic figure, agreement table and three additional boxplots, alongside conference-format layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful controls, annotation-reliability evidence and diagnostic analyses, but removes explicit limitations and several comparisons. Moreover, Section 4.5 retains the 15.28-point average transfer gain supported by v1's unfine-tuned baseline, whereas revised Table 3 implies approximately 1.93 points against the new no-extension baseline. The stronger comparisons therefore coexist with materially misleading interpretation and reduced qualification, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
